_readme: Every source starts disabled. Run `prepare_malaysia.py inspect --repo <repo>` (hub) or open the file (table/manifest), fix files/columns, then set enabled true. Licences were taken from search results, not verified: read each card before use, and before any commercial use.

sources.name: mesolitica_stt_whisper
sources.license: licence not stated in search results: check the card. Malaysian speech with Malay/English code-switching; Mandarin/Tamil rows are dropped by the script filter
sources._note: If audio sits in zip files instead of parquet bytes, download and unzip it, set audio_root to that folder, or convert to a manifest source

sources.name: malaya_speech_malay_stt
sources.license: licence not stated in search results: check the card. Transcripts are largely machine-labelled (semi-supervised), so expect noise

sources.name: fleurs_ms_train
sources.license: CC-BY-4.0. Formal read Malay, about 9.5 h. No speaker id, so it cannot be speaker-split; use fleurs_ms_test for scoring

sources.name: fleurs_ms_test
sources.license: CC-BY-4.0. Formal read Malay test set, about 2.3 h. Never train on it

sources.name: commonvoice_ms_spontaneous
sources.license: CC0 (Common Voice Spontaneous Speech 3.0, ms-MY, about 6 h). Colloquial, unscripted. Download from Mozilla Data Collective; adjust path/columns to the files you get

sources.name: commonvoice_ms_scripted
sources.license: CC0 (Common Voice Scripted Speech, ms, about 3.6 h, very little validated)

sources.name: imda_nsc
sources.license: Singapore Open Data Licence (commercial use on request). Singapore English, the closest large open source to Manglish. Download from IMDA and convert its transcripts to a JSONL manifest with a speaker field

sources.name: magichub_malcsc
sources.license: Reported CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: research only. 5 h conversational Malay from MagicHub

sources.name: revolab_benchmark
sources.license: Annotations CC-BY-4.0, audio under original terms; gated (accept terms on the Hub). Malay/English code-switching, about 2.2 h. Evaluation only
